name: Question 7
problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by the unit circle and the coordinate axes in the first quadrant. Express ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$  where $F(x,y)=⟨y\operatorname{cos}⁡x,x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}}⟩,$ as a repeated integral.
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14061381/assets/e48034aed1f41cf1f9b30c057186879233fe05cd2ba720dcee436398a732b6ce.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}})\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $Q(x,y)=x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the closed curve C, which is the boundary of the region enclosed by the unit circle and the coordinate axes in the first quadrant. Express ∮CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=⟨ycos⁡x,x−e−y2⟩, as a repeated integral.

a
∫01∫01−x2(1+ysin⁡x)dydx
b
∫01∫01−x2(1−cos⁡x)dydx
c
∫01∫−1−x21−x2(1+cos⁡x)dydx
d
∫−11∫01−x2(1+cos⁡x)dydx
e
∫−11∫−1−x21−x2(1−cos⁡x)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let C be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let D be the region bounded by C. If P and Q have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing D, then Green's theorem states that ∮CPdx+Qdy=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA.

The region D and the curve C for this case are shown below.

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows: ∮CF⋅dr=∮Cycos⁡xdx+(x−e−y2)dy

We have that P(x,y)=ycos⁡x and Q(x,y)=x−e−y2. Therefore, ∂P∂y=cos⁡x,∂Q∂x=1.

We can express the region D as a type I region as follows: D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−x2}

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get ∮Cycos⁡xdx+(x−e−y2)dy=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA=∬D(1−cos⁡x)dA=∫01∫01−x2(1−cos⁡x)dydx.
